item.title: French presidential candidate Mélenchon joins protest in Paris

item.content:encoded:
French presidential candidate Mélenchon joins protest in Paris Jean-Luc Mélenchon, the France Unbowed (La France Insoumise) candidate for the 2027 French presidential election, on Saturday participated in the demonstration as the protest against the rising cost of living in the country enters its third weekend, according to France24. ANI | Updated: 31-10-2026 21:02 IST | Created: 31-10-2026 21:02 IST

France Unbowed leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon joins nationwide protests (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Jean-Luc Mélenchon, the France Unbowed (La France Insoumise) candidate for the 2027 French presidential election, on Saturday participated in the demonstration as the protest against the rising cost of living in the country enters its third weekend, according to France24. The left-wing leader Mélenchon had also joined the protests on October 24, last weekend. According to the French media outlet, about 15,000 people joined the demonstrations today, while the Interior Ministry noted that the events unfolded "without any notable incidents”. Police have made 27 arrests by 2:00 pm (local time), in contrast to 217 arrests a week ago. The country witnessed heightened security as protests coincided with Halloween, deploying around 70,000 security personnel amid fears that demonstrators could use festive masks to conceal their identities. French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez had warned of a "very high risk" of unrest, assuring that authorities would respond firmly to any violence. "Everyone is on deck to ensure an extremely firm response to any trouble," Nunez said at a news conference earlier this week, outlining security arrangements for Saturday. France24 reported that the transportation authorities closed several metro and suburban stations in the Paris metropolitan area, with more than 40 stations affected. The demonstrations in France gained momentum in late September as President Emmanuel Macron's minority government began discussions on the 2027 budget. With public debt approaching 120 per cent of economic output and borrowing costs rising, the government faces mounting pressure to reduce spending. Students protesting the deteriorating condition of schools, overcrowded classrooms and an admissions system widely perceived as unfair have been joined by trade unions and members of the resurgent 'Yellow Vest' movement, which is demanding action on the cost of living. Meanwhile in Germany today, the protesters took to the streets under the banner of campaign group "Gen Z regelt" (Gen Z takes charge). As per France24, the protesters oppose compulsory military service and demand more investment in education amid inflation. Currently, there is a wider wave of youth-led demonstrations across Europe, with protesters raising concerns over the cost of living, declining educational facilities, social inequality and diminishing economic prospects. (ANI)

Iran claims US struck fishing boats off Qeshm Island, two injured As reported by the news agency IRNA, the two fishermen who went missing after the drone attack have been found, according to the CEO of the Qeshm Fishing Community. Both were sent back to Qeshm Island. ANI | Updated: 31-10-2026 18:39 IST | Created: 31-10-2026 18:39 IST

Representative image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

Iran

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The United States reportedly struck two fishing boats off Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, injuring two Iranian fishermen. As reported by the news agency IRNA, the two fishermen who went missing after the drone attack have been found, according to the CEO of the Qeshm Fishing Community. Both were sent back to Qeshm Island. Meanwhile, one of the two injured fishermen was taken to a hospital, Al Jazeera reported, citing Fars news agency. “This incident occurred around 11:30 am today involving two fishing boats within 18 miles of the village of Musan, affiliated with Qeshm County… Each boat had two occupants,” the deputy governor of Hormozgan Province for political, security, and social affairs told Tasnim news agency, as per Al Jazeera. As strikes continue in the Strait of Hormuz, earlier, Iranian naval forces destroyed an "enemy submarine" and damaged two commercial oil tankers in the operational zone east of Hormuz on Friday morning. State media Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB) reported, citing the Iranian Navy's Public Relations department, that Iranian forces targeted and destroyed an adversary submarine navigating the operational sector near the vital maritime choke point. "This morning, an enemy submarine that was operating in the operational area east of the Strait of Hormuz was hit and destroyed by Iranian Navy sailors," the Navy statement read. Meanwhile, the Commander of the United States Central Command (CENTCOM), Admiral Brad Cooper, on Friday (local time) stated that the primary internationally recognised transit routes in the Strait of Hormuz have been successfully cleared of Iranian sea mines and commercial vessels are sailing freely through the strategic waterway. "Earlier this week, I visited some of the more than 50,000 service members supporting operations across the Middle East, including our mission in the Strait of Hormuz. When I flew over the strait, I saw dozens of commercial vessels transiting—all types: cargo, crude oil, liquid natural gas, or LNG. And I also saw our U.S. assets in the air and on the water, including a squadron of advanced sea drones that were on patrol, supporting a defensive layer," Admiral Cooper stated. This comes as the possibility of fresh strikes lurks in Iran. Today, Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei ordered senior commanders to confront all the threats “with an immediate, effective, and unrestricted geographical response.” According to a series of X posts by the account of Mojtaba Khamenei, the Iranian leader met with senior commanders of the armed forces against the backdrop of possibilities of fresh escalation between the United States and Iran. “Every level and type of threat must be confronted with an immediate, effective, and unrestricted geographical response,” the statement read. (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
Iran: Mojtaba Khamenei orders "effective, unrestricted geographical response" if US strikes According to a series of X posts by the account of Mojtaba Khamenei, the Iranian leader met with senior commanders of the armed forces against the backdrop of possibilities of fresh escalation between the United States and Iran. ANI | Updated: 31-10-2026 17:08 IST | Created: 31-10-2026 17:08 IST

Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei (File photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

Iran

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has ordered senior commanders to confront all the threats “with an immediate, effective, and unrestricted geographical response.” According to a series of X posts by the account of Mojtaba Khamenei, the Iranian leader met with senior commanders of the armed forces against the backdrop of possibilities of fresh escalation between the United States and Iran. “Every level and type of threat must be confronted with an immediate, effective, and unrestricted geographical response,” the statement read. In a strongly worded statement, he instructed the armed forces to retaliate in case the military attacks resume. “If the enemies resume military or terrorist attacks, it is the armed forces of the Islamic Republic and the people of Iran who will determine the time and conditions for ending them,” he said. He emphasised an “intelligent combat readiness to confront the enemies with force” as a requirement of “maximum deterrence”. Khamenei also directed the forces to strengthen Iran’s defence technology. Earlier, US President Trump stated that Washington is in no hurry to end its war with Iran, characterising the ongoing hostilities as "not a typical war" while maintaining that time favours the American side despite months of fighting and repeated diplomatic efforts failing to yield a lasting settlement. “There are talks. They want to talk. They keep talking,” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office. “But look, they're not paying their soldiers, they're not paying their police. They're in a lot of trouble. And we have time, frankly. It's a war, but it's not a typical war; we've been there for seven months,” the US President added. However, there is a preliminary draft framework for US-Iran negotiations, which proposes transferring Iran's highly enriched uranium stockpile to an agreed third country or reducing its enrichment level, while reopening the Strait of Hormuz to international maritime traffic within seven days of an initial understanding, Al Arabiya English reported. According to Al Arabiya English, which exclusively obtained the draft's key points, China could potentially act as a guarantor for the implementation and sustainability of any agreement. The framework also proposes holding direct US-Iran negotiations in Doha instead of Istanbul. An American delegation is expected to join Iranian officials for direct talks in Doha following a reported breakthrough in indirect negotiations, The Times of Israel reported, citing the Qatari newspaper Al-Araby Al-Jadeed. (ANI)

item.title: Binance sets aside USD 6.34 billion to cover crypto hack losses, targets phased withdrawal resumption
item.description: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has set aside more than USD 6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses from the USD 6.3 billion security breach, with about 80 per cent of the stolen token assets ...
item.content:encoded:
Binance sets aside USD 6.34 billion to cover crypto hack losses, targets phased withdrawal resumption Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has set aside more than USD 6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses from the USD 6.3 billion security breach, with about 80 per cent of the stolen token assets already replenished, as the company works to restore withdrawal services in phases. ANI | Updated: 31-10-2026 15:44 IST | Created: 31-10-2026 15:44 IST

Binance Logo (Photo/Binance). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has set aside more than USD 6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses from the USD 6.3 billion security breach, with about 80 per cent of the stolen token assets already replenished, as the company works to restore withdrawal services in phases. In its second security incident recovery update, Binance said it would absorb the entire financial impact of the theft through its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and corporate treasury, ensuring users do not bear the losses. "We want to be clear about our commitment: Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users," the exchange said in the statement. The company said it had already secured USD 5 billion in the same digital assets that were stolen, including USDC, USDT, Bitcoin (BTC), Ether (ETH) and BNB. "This means that we have already covered approximately 80% of the impacted amount. We are actively buying the remaining relevant token assets through market and OTC channels," Binance said. The exchange confirmed that its hot wallets were compromised at around 20:05 UTC on October 29, resulting in unauthorised withdrawals of approximately USD 6.3 billion worth of digital assets. As part of its recovery efforts, Binance said approximately USD 3 billion in stolen assets had been frozen on blockchain networks through coordination with law enforcement agencies, blockchain intelligence firms, asset issuers and industry partners. The company also provided a timeline for restoring services, saying its technical team was targeting the phased resumption of withdrawals within approximately 34 hours, subject to the completion of security checks. Deposits and other unaffected platform services remain operational, it said. Binance further announced plans to publish an updated Proof of Reserves report by Monday, November 2, to allow users to verify the digital assets backing their account balances. On the cause of the breach, the exchange said its initial investigation had pointed to a compromised laptop, but subsequent findings revealed additional points of intrusion. "Our initial investigation suggested that the incident may involve a compromised laptop, however, our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach," it said. The company reiterated that it had found no evidence of wallet private keys being leaked and said further technical findings were expected within approximately 48 hours, subject to verification. Meanwhile, according to Reuters, blockchain investigation firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis have linked the USD 6.3 billion theft to a North Korean hacking group known as TraderTraitor. Cybersecurity experts cited by Reuters said proceeds from North Korean cryptocurrency thefts have helped fund the country's weapons programmes. Binance has not publicly confirmed who was responsible for the attack and said its investigation remains ongoing. The exchange said it would publish a detailed technical report outlining how the breach occurred and the additional security measures being introduced to prevent similar incidents. (ANI)
